summary: WAVES is a two-year Erasmus Mundus master's in water vulnerability engineering, run by the University of Twente (ITC) in the Netherlands, the University of Padova and the University of Ljubljana. Eighteen scholarships for 2027 cover tuition, insurance and field work and pay €1,400 a month. Applications close on 15 January 2027 at 23:59 CET, and there is never an application fee.
meta_title: WAVES 2027: Erasmus Mundus water engineering scholarship
meta_description: WAVES gives 18 scholarships with tuition, insurance and €1,400 a month for a water engineering master's in Twente, Padova and Ljubljana. Apply by 15 January.
covers: Tuition and participation costs in full, including health and accident insurance. Self-funded non-EU students pay €12,000 a year.
€1,400 a month for living costs for 24 months.
eligibility: Applicants of any nationality who have not held an Erasmus Mundus scholarship before.

A bachelor's of at least 180 ECTS in engineering, geosciences, environmental sciences, geography, physics, mathematics or a related field, including at least 58 ECTS across mathematics, physics, chemistry, hydraulics or fluid mechanics, programming or numerical methods, solid mechanics, and hydraulic structures, sanitary engineering or geotechnics. There is no conditional admission.

English: IELTS Academic 6.5 with no band below 6.0, or TOEFL, Cambridge, PTE or LanguageCert equivalents. Ghana and Nigeria get a conditional exemption: at least three years of in-person higher education taught fully in English, stated on your transcript, diploma supplement or an official letter.
how_to_apply: Apply on the WAVES portal, open since 13 October 2026, by 15 January 2027 at 23:59 CET.
Choose a track: Spatial Water Sciences (Padova, then Twente), Water Vulnerability Engineering (Ljubljana, then Padova) or Spatial Water Governance and Policy (Ljubljana, then Twente).

Upload your bachelor's certificate (or expected graduation statement), full transcript with grading scale, a two-page CV in English, proof of English, your passport and, for a scholarship, proof of residence for the last five years.
Recorded interviews run in February and March 2027, and offers must be confirmed by 17 April 2027.
watch_out: Check your transcript against the 58 ECTS of foundation subjects before applying: they are strict.
A transcript that only says 'medium of instruction: English' is not enough by itself; it must show the teaching was fully in English.
Your passport must be valid for at least 18 months after the programme starts on 1 October 2027.
There is never a fee to apply.
costs: Tuition (€12,000 a year for non-EU students)
documents: Bachelor's certificate or expected graduation statement
CV in English, two pages maximum
Passport valid 18 months after the start
Proof of residence for the last five years (scholarship applicants)

faq.a: 15 January 2027 at 23:59 CET, for both scholarship and self-funded applicants.
